verses.commentary: Twenty first day of seventh month, nearly a month into construction. On the last day of the Feast of Tabernacles, when Israel remembers wilderness wanderings and anticipates harvest rest.
Same addressees: Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant. Continuity of audience signals continuity of concern. God stays engaged with his servants.
Who remembers Solomon's temple? Older survivors would recall its glory. The new structure looks like nothing in comparison. Discouragement threatens the project. Memory can be burden or blessing.

Be strong. Three times repeated for Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the people. And work. The command joins strength to action. 'For I am with you' provides the foundation. Divine presence enables human effort.

The covenant from Egypt remains in force. The Spirit (ruach) stands among them. Do not fear. Exodus liberation, covenant promise, and Spirit presence all reassure. Past faithfulness guarantees future help.
In a little while, cosmic shaking. Heaven, earth, sea, dry land all tremble. God's sovereignty extends beyond Israel to all creation. The shaking prepares for greater glory.

All nations shaken. 'What is desired by all nations' will come (or 'the treasures of all nations'). This house filled with glory. Messianic interpretations see Christ as the desire of nations. The humble temple becomes the site of ultimate revelation.
Silver and gold belong to God. Resources are not the issue. The Lord of all possesses all. Human poverty cannot limit divine glory. What God wills, God supplies.

Greater glory in the latter house than the former. Solomon's temple exceeded in this modest structure? Only if something greater than architecture is measured. Peace (shalom) promised in this place. The temple that saw Jesus knew peace the first temple never experienced.
New date: twenty fourth day of ninth month, second year of Darius. Three months into building. God tests understanding through questions.
Ask the priests about the law. Teaching is their responsibility. God uses existing religious structures to convey truth. The question sets up an important lesson.
Consecrated meat in a garment fold: does the holiness transfer to bread, stew, wine, oil, or food? The priests correctly answer no. Holiness does not automatically spread through contact.

Reverse question. Corpse defilement through contact: does it make things unclean? The priests correctly answer yes. Uncleanness spreads more easily than holiness. Corruption is contagious; righteousness is not.
Application: so it is with this people and nation. Their defilement spreads to everything they do and offer. Contaminated hands produce contaminated gifts. The problem is internal, not external.
Give careful thought again. Consider conditions before construction began. Before one stone was laid on another. Haggai invites comparison between neglect and obedience.
Expected twenty measures, got ten. Expected fifty measures of wine, got twenty. Yield reduced by half. Mathematical precision demonstrates divine discipline. Disobedience halved productivity.

God struck their work with blight, mildew, and hail. Agricultural plagues. Yet you did not return to me. Divine discipline intended to provoke repentance met resistance. Judgment alone does not transform.
From this day forward, from the twenty fourth of the ninth month, when the temple foundation was laid. Mark this date. Consider carefully. A turning point begins.
Is seed still in the barn? Have vine, fig, pomegranate, and olive borne fruit? Present scarcity acknowledged. But from this day forward, blessing promised. Obedience reverses the curse.
Same day, second word to Haggai. Doubled communication emphasizes importance. God has more to say to Zerubbabel specifically.
Tell Zerubbabel: heaven and earth will shake. The cosmic shaking from verse 6 repeated. What applies to nations applies to all creation. God's sovereignty spans every domain.
Royal thrones overturned, foreign power shattered. Chariots and riders fall. Brother turns on brother. Military strength collapses. Empire becomes chaos. Human kingdoms serve divine timetables.

On that day, Zerubbabel becomes God's signet ring (chotam). A signet ring represents authority and identity. What Jehoiachin lost (Jeremiah 22:24), Zerubbabel regains. The Davidic line restored, pointing forward to Christ. I have chosen you. Election secures destiny. The book ends with messianic hope.
